camera.enable_notes: Run docker-wyze-bridge with the Wyze account and developer API Key/ID. Select a supported cloud product/model and manually supply the bridge/NVR host. These streams are not served by the camera's own address.

streams.name: Local RTSP (via bridge)
streams.notes: {address} is the bridge/NVR host; {camera_name} is the bridge slug.

streams.name: Local HLS (via bridge)
streams.notes: Actual MediaMTX HLS playlist path on the bridge/NVR host.

discovery.none: No automatic bridge discovery is documented. Cameras are enumerated from the owner's Wyze cloud account, not through an on-LAN _http8554 service. Ask the user for the bridge/NVR hostname or address and the camera's bridge slug; do not substitute the camera's own IP for {address}.

identification.notes: There is no camera-discovery matcher in this spec. Select a supported cloud product/model and manually supply the bridge/NVR host. In particular, the bridge does not advertise _http._tcp on port 8554.

device.name: Wyze Cam (via docker-wyze-bridge)
device.notes:
On stock firmware these cameras have no first-party general-purpose local API. The exception is the separate, model- and firmware-specific official RTSP branch documented in wyze-legacy-rtsp.yaml; that exception must not be generalized to other firmware or models.
The community docker-wyze-bridge authenticates to the Wyze cloud and uses each camera's cloud-issued TUTK values, then serves media on the bridge/NVR host. This spec declares the generic RTSP and HLS endpoints only. WebRTC is omitted because six allowed models are in the pinned NO_WEBRTC set and the stream schema cannot scope a template by variant. A Wyze account and developer API Key/ID are required; this is not an account-free or permanently cloud-isolated path. The bridge prefers a LAN upstream connection but can fall back to P2P or relay. The RTSP/HLS endpoints below are still local to the bridge host even when that upstream path is relayed.
identify_only reflects this project's missing video-player integration, not the bridge's capabilities. {address} is always the manually configured bridge/NVR host, never the camera address. A consumer with a player can use the opaque per-camera slug and authentication facts below.

openness.notes: Wyze publishes no general local API for stock firmware. The bridge is an independent implementation of the TUTK transport and a local media server.

exclusivity.recovery: A camera belongs to one Wyze account. Remove it from the old account or use its exact reset procedure before adding it elsewhere. Close other TUTK clients if the bridge reports that the camera's session limit was reached; the numeric limit is not established here.

pairing.notes: No Bluetooth-style pairing window exists. Cloud-issued camera values and local bridge credentials are separate app-layer gates.

pin.notes: There is no camera PIN. The cloud supplies the per-camera TUTK identity and secret to the bridge after account/developer-API authentication. Consumer-to-bridge authorization is independently controlled by WB_AUTH/WB_API and STREAM_AUTH as declared in protocol_details.bridge_authentication.

unpair.clears: The bridge's cloud/API authorization, or the camera's account binding when removed in the vendor app.
unpair.notes: Revoke the Wyze developer API key and clear cached bridge credentials to cut off that bridge. Remove the camera in the vendor app to release its account binding. Also rotate WB_API/STREAM_AUTH secrets when a stream consumer must lose access; revoking cloud access alone does not change credentials already configured on the local media server.

issued_to_client: Wyze account session and developer API Key/ID for the bridge
Bridge WB_PASSWORD and unique WB_API key
credentials.notes: The bridge obtains per-camera TUTK values from the cloud device list. WB_API and stream credentials are separate from the Wyze developer API Key/ID. Keep all of them secret and never expose the media ports to an untrusted network.
stored_on_device: Per-camera TUTK values issued through the Wyze account

factory_reset.description: Wyze gives Cam v1 a 20-second hold and the other three covered cameras a 10-second hold. Do not apply a generic hold to every bridge variant, and do not use a factory reset as a routine bridge reconnect step.
factory_reset.effect: Deletes the camera's settings file and returns it to setup. Remove the microSD card first; cloud recordings are outside this procedure. These procedures cover only standalone Cam v1, v2, v3 and Pan v1, not the other supported bridge products and not Floodlight v1 despite its shared WYZE_CAKP2JFUS model code.

procedures.basis: Wyze's factory-reset article for Cam v1/v2/v3/Pan v1 and the Cam v1 QSG.
procedures.indicator: Solid yellow changes to blinking yellow.
procedures.name: Cam v1 Setup button held for 20 seconds

steps.action: Remove any microSD card. With the Cam v1 powered, hold its bottom Setup button for 20 seconds.
Release and wait at least 30 seconds, allowing up to five minutes, until the light changes from solid yellow to blinking yellow.

procedures.basis: Wyze's factory-reset article for Cam v1/v2/v3/Pan v1 and the Cam v2/Pan v1 QSGs.
procedures.indicator: Solid yellow changes to blinking yellow.
procedures.name: Cam v2 or Pan v1 Setup button held for 10 seconds

steps.action: Remove any microSD card. With the Cam v2 or Pan v1 powered, hold its bottom Setup button for 10 seconds.
Release and wait at least 30 seconds, allowing up to five minutes, until the light changes from solid yellow to blinking yellow.

procedures.basis: Wyze's factory-reset article for Cam v1/v2/v3/Pan v1 and the standalone Cam v3 QSG.
procedures.name: Standalone Cam v3 Setup button held for 10 seconds

steps.action: Confirm this is a standalone Cam v3, not Floodlight v1. Remove any microSD card and hold the powered camera's bottom Setup button for 10 seconds.
Release and wait at least 30 seconds, allowing up to five minutes, until the status light turns red and the camera is ready to set up again.

cloud.local_alternative: Partial only: LAN mode keeps the upstream media on the LAN when it succeeds, and every re-served endpoint is on the bridge host. Wyze account/API access remains required and permanent isolation is not supported. NET_MODE=LAN rejects non-LAN upstream sessions rather than making the camera independent of the cloud.
cloud.provider: Wyze cloud and Wyze developer API

methods.description: Onboard a listed camera in the Wyze app, configure the bridge with the same account's email/password and developer API Key/ID, then consume streams on the bridge host. There is no account-free alternative.
methods.name: Wyze cloud credentials and a community bridge

steps.action: Confirm that the exact product and model code appear in device.variants; do not try an excluded Gwell, Meari, Battery Cam Pro, Floodlight Pro, Doorbell Pro or HL_PAN4 product.
Onboard the camera to a Wyze account in the vendor app.
Create a Wyze developer API Key and API ID and configure docker-wyze-bridge with those values and the account email/password.
Leave the default LAN preference, or set NET_MODE=LAN to reject P2P and relay sessions; do not describe either choice as permanent offline support.
Manually configure the bridge/NVR host as {address}, derive {camera_name} with protocol_details.camera_slug, and use the selected local stream URL with the configured authentication.
steps.expect: The bridge serves the camera on RTSP 8554 or HLS 8888, subject to its authentication configuration. No generic WebRTC endpoint is offered; see protocol_details.webrtc_scope.

setup.notes: Camera onboarding, camera enumeration and TUTK credentials all depend on the Wyze account/cloud. Cached bridge tokens may survive a restart, but permanent cloud isolation is explicitly unsupported upstream.

rejoin.notes: Use the exact model's Wyze app setup/reconnect flow, then let the bridge rediscover the account device. A factory reset is not the default network-change procedure; if one becomes necessary, use only the matching procedure above. The bridge/NVR host may also need its own address updated in the client.

testing.notes: No camera or bridge was driven by this project. Supported models, TUTK session modes, stream URLs, slug construction and authentication are reported from docker-wyze-bridge; reset procedures come from Wyze support.

variants.notes: The model code is shared. HL_CFL is only the Floodlight v1 accessory identity that distinguishes it from standalone Cam v3; it is not a standalone cloud camera model or variant. Use the cloud product and accessory identity, especially for reset, and do not infer Floodlight Pro from either code.

artifacts.description: Source for models, stream behavior, slugs and authentication; the SHA is the reviewed Git commit, not a file digest.

evidence.documentation_review: The supported-camera allowlist is transcribed from README lines 161-188 at the pinned bridge revision. Authentication and network-mode behavior were checked against the project wikis and public implementation. Wyze's current factory-reset article supplies the v1-specific 20-second hold and the 10-second hold for the other three covered products.
evidence.open_questions: Exact per-firmware TUTK reliability, maximum concurrent camera sessions and how long cached credentials can survive without cloud access remain unverified. Additional WebRTC/ICE and host/network behavior also remains unverified; the six NO_WEBRTC model exclusions are known and declared.

covers: RTSP and HLS served by the manually configured bridge/NVR host
not_covered: A guarantee of LAN-only upstream media unless NET_MODE=LAN is enforced
A generic WebRTC stream, because six allowed models are explicitly in the pinned NO_WEBRTC set and stream entries cannot be variant-scoped
local_access.summary: Stock cameras can use TUTK LAN mode through the community bridge, whose media endpoints are local. Account/API bootstrapping and continuing cloud dependence remain; permanent isolation is unsupported.

custom_stream_auth.behavior: Each entry can grant a user all paths or only named camera slugs. An empty username matches any username, so an empty username/password creates an anonymous grant with optional IP/path restrictions. These STREAM_AUTH grants can coexist with WB_AUTH=true and its WB_API credential; both mechanisms are configured.
custom_stream_auth.restriction_semantics: Empty client_ips means any client IP and empty paths means every camera path. The examples below use invented credentials and documentation-only addresses.

default.rest_api: The WB_API key is accepted in the api query parameter or api header.
default.stream_password_source: The unique WB_API key shown at the bottom of the bridge Web UI, or an explicitly configured WB_API value.
default.webui_password_source: WB_PASSWORD; if unset, the bridge derives it from the Wyze email local part.

whole_stream_default_anonymous.behavior: This specific whole-stream default-anonymous configuration adds an anonymous MediaMTX read user for every stream; it is not the only way to configure anonymous or IP/path-restricted access.
whole_stream_default_anonymous.warning: This is a deliberate insecure choice for a trusted isolated LAN, not the default and not safe port-forwarding exposure.

algorithm: Trim leading/trailing whitespace from the Wyze nickname (or use the MAC when no nickname exists).
Replace every ASCII space with a hyphen.
Apply the upstream default-name filter: retain ASCII letters, digits, underscore, hyphen and plus; remove other non-ASCII/special characters.
camera_slug.overrides_out_of_scope: URI_SEPARATOR and URI_MAC can change upstream names; this spec uses the unmodified default only.

excluded: All Gwell models, including GW_GC1 and GW_GC2
supported_camera_scope.rule: Allow only device.variants and their listed products. Unknown, warning-marked and different-SDK products are denied, not experimental matches.

tutk_sessions.default: ANY tries LAN first, then can fall back to P2P or relay.
tutk_sessions.lan_only: NET_MODE=LAN rejects any session whose numeric mode is not 2.

modes.meaning: Direct peer-to-peer upstream path over the internet.
modes.name: P2P

modes.meaning: Upstream media relayed through Wyze servers; local bridge endpoints do not move into the cloud.
modes.name: relay

modes.meaning: Upstream media flows directly between camera and bridge on the LAN.
modes.name: LAN

webrtc_scope.reason: The pinned bridge has a NO_WEBRTC model set, while camera.streams has no supported per-variant exclusion field. Omit the generic WebRTC template rather than offer it on known-unsupported models.
webrtc_scope.remaining_unknown: Only additional WebRTC/ICE and host/network behavior remains unknown; the six NO_WEBRTC model exclusions are known and are not open questions.

remaining_unknowns: No supported camera was streamed through the bridge by this project.
The duration and failure mode of operation during an extended cloud outage are not established.
Additional WebRTC/ICE and host/network behavior and per-model substream support remain unknown; the six NO_WEBRTC model exclusions are known, not unknown.
Reset procedures for every non-v1/v2/v3/Pan-v1 bridge variant are deliberately not established here.
